task.role:
You are setting up Claude Studio on a machine that has never run it. Claude Studio is a console-driven video editor: a recording goes in, a vertical 1080x1920 short with burned-in TikTok-style captions comes out — transcribed, silence-trimmed, and rendered in one command. It is built on Remotion (video as React components) and AssemblyAI (word-level transcription).
The repository is the entire system. Your job is to clone it, install it, wire in one API key, and prove it renders — not to design or rewrite anything. After cloning, the repo's own CLAUDE.md is the authority on how the code works; read it and defer to it wherever it is more specific than this prompt.

inputs.repo_url: FILL IN: git URL, or the path to a .bundle file copied onto this machine
inputs.target_dir: FILL IN: where to clone, e.g. ~/Videos/claude-studio
inputs.assemblyai_key: FILL IN, or leave blank and stop to ask the human at step 3

task.preconditions:
Check these before touching anything, and report all failures together rather than one at a time.
The scripts in scripts/ are .mts files executed directly by Node via native TypeScript type stripping. There is no build step and no ts-node. The npm scripts pass no --experimental-strip-types flag, so stripping must be on by default: Node 22.18+ or 23.6+. 24 LTS is the safe answer. Anything older cannot run them at all. If the version is too old, stop and tell the human — do not install a Node version manager or upgrade their system Node without being asked.
Needed to clone.
Needs roughly 2 GB free. npm install pulls a Chrome build and an ffmpeg build for Remotion.
System ffmpeg is not required — Remotion bundles its own. It is worth having for inspecting sources and building proxies, because Remotion's bundled build has most filters compiled out. Note its absence; do not install it unprompted.

procedure.step: Clone repo_url into target_dir. A .bundle path clones exactly like a URL: `git clone claude-studio.bundle claude-studio`. Work in that directory from here on.

Run `npm i`. Expect several minutes and a large download on first run. Do not add, remove, or upgrade any dependency. Remotion's packages are version-locked to each other and must only ever move as a set, via `npm run upgrade`.

`cp .env.example .env`, then write the AssemblyAI key into it on the `ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY=` line.
If assemblyai_key was left blank, stop here and ask the human for it. Do not invent a placeholder, do not skip ahead to the render steps, and do not commit .env — it is gitignored and must stay that way.
Then offer, but do not assume: cp corrections.example.json corrections.json # misheard word -> right spelling cp overlays.example.json overlays.json # keyword -> image shown when spoken Both are gitignored personal config. corrections.json is worth creating early: the transcriber reliably mishears brand and product names, and a fix there survives every re-run.

Read CLAUDE.md and README.md now, before running anything else. CLAUDE.md documents the two architectural boundaries that matter (src vs scripts, scripts/lib vs scripts/*.mts), the caption mapping subtlety, the silence cut, and a set of render traps that no automated check catches. You will need it for step 6.

task.verification:
Run these gates in order, cheapest first. Each catches a different class of failure. Do not report the install as working until gate 4 has passed and you have looked at the image from gate 5.
Pure logic: the caption mapping, the silence cut, chaining, the clip window, corrections, ducking, overlays. No API call, no render, no key needed. Must print `ok`.
eslint over src and scripts, plus tsc. Must exit clean.
Must list exactly one composition: `Captions`. That id is the public handle the CLI and any script look it up by.
The cheapest proof that the webpack bundle, headless Chrome, and the encoder all work together. Roughly 10-20 seconds. It renders the committed fixture — public/sample.mp3 and its transcript in public/captions.json — so it passes before any of the human's own media exists.
Layout and timing bugs survive all four gates above. Render this still and actually look at the image.
Expected: white uppercase Montserrat captions, one word highlighted in yellow (#fde047), sitting in the lower third, over black.
Three failures and what each means — all three are documented in CLAUDE.md: - Nothing visible at all: the captions were painted underneath the positioned video layer. They must live in their own AbsoluteFill. - One word per line: AbsoluteFill is flex-direction column; the caption block needs flex-row. - Wrong typeface: the loadFont call from @remotion/google-fonts/Montserrat at module scope in CaptionedVideo.tsx is not taking effect, and the render fell back to whatever font this machine happens to have.
task.handoff:
Once every gate passes, show the human how to make their first short:
npm run short -- their-recording.mp4 --lang=es
Tell them plainly: every positional argument is an input played in order, the output is named with --out= and defaults to out/short.mp4, and a render with video behind the captions takes minutes rather than seconds because OffthreadVideo extracts each frame with ffmpeg. Point them at README.md for the full flag table.
Delete out/smoke.mp4 and out/frame.png, or say that you left them.
task.known_traps:
Found the hard way on the machine this repo came from. None are visible in the code.
`npm run short` uploads each input to AssemblyAI whole — video track included — and renders from that same file. Modern camera footage is a bad fit for both: drone and phone clips are commonly 4K or 3K, 10-bit HEVC, 48-60 fps, and hundreds of megabytes per minute. That is a slow upload followed by a much slower render.
Build 1080x1920 proxies first. The composition renders at 1080x1920 regardless, so the downscale costs nothing that would have survived anyway:
ffmpeg -y -i source.MP4 -map 0:v:0 -map 0:a:0 \ -vf scale=1080:1920 -r 30 \ -c:v libx264 -preset fast -crf 20 -pix_fmt yuv420p \ -c:a aac -b:a 192k public/clip-01.mp4
Measured on this footage: 1.4 GB of 3K HEVC became 143 MB.
On an Intel iGPU (Tiger Lake), VAAPI transcoded all 9 clips — 135 seconds of 3K HEVC — in about a minute. The same job on libx264 at `-preset medium -crf 18` had not finished the first 17-second clip after eight minutes and was abandoned, so the exact ratio is unmeasured; the order of magnitude is not. Try hardware first.
ffmpeg -y -hwaccel vaapi -hwaccel_device /dev/dri/renderD128 \ -hwaccel_output_format vaapi -i source.MP4 -map 0:v:0 -map 0:a:0 \ -vf 'scale_vaapi=w=1080:h=1920:format=nv12,fps=30' \ -c:v h264_vaapi -qp 23 -c:a aac -b:a 192k public/clip-01.mp4
Check with `ls /dev/dri/` and `ffmpeg -encoders | grep vaapi`. Two details are not optional: - `format=nv12` — without it a 10-bit source dies with `No usable encoding profile found`, because h264_vaapi cannot accept the 10-bit surface the decoder produced. - `-map 0:v:0` — camera files often carry an extra MJPEG thumbnail video stream that ffmpeg would otherwise try to encode as well. An `hevc_nvenc` entry in the encoder list means only that ffmpeg was built with it; confirm the GPU actually exists with `lspci | grep -i vga` before relying on it.
A render's progress counter is written with carriage returns. Piping it through `tail`, `head`, or any non-line-buffered filter hides every line until the process exits, so a 12-minute render looks identical to a hung one. Let render output through unfiltered, or watch it with a line-buffered grep.
Check the transcript before rendering, not after. `public/captions.json` is written before the render starts, so a wrong brand name can be fixed there and re-rendered with `npm run render -- Captions out/x.mp4` — no second transcription, no second API charge. Add the fix to corrections.json at the same time so it never comes back. Matching is whole-word and case-insensitive, and single-word only.
Every `npm run short` and `npm run transcribe` overwrites public/captions.json. The committed one is the sample fixture's real transcript. Copy it aside if a transcript still matters.

constraints.do: Read CLAUDE.md before changing any code, and follow it where it is more specific than this prompt.
Run the gates in order and report the actual output, including failures.
Look at the image in gate 5. It is the only check that sees a layout bug.
Stop and ask when the API key is missing, when Node is too old, or when a gate fails for a reason you cannot explain.
constraints.do_not: Do not upgrade, add, or remove dependencies. Remotion's packages move as a set, through `npm run upgrade` only.
Do not commit .env, corrections.json, overlays.json, out/, or any media in public/. All are gitignored deliberately.
Do not rename the `Captions` composition id. It is the public handle every render command uses.
Do not import from src/ into scripts/ beyond the pure modules src/lib/silence.ts, framing.ts, ducking.ts, and overlays.ts. That boundary is deliberate and documented.

Do not introduce Date.now(), Math.random(), or wall-clock animation into anything under src/. Remotion renders each frame as a deterministic snapshot; the same frame number must always produce the same pixels.
Do not build an agent binary, a web layer, or a Lambda deployment as part of setup. CLAUDE.md explains why each is deferred.
